t: First aid for the prepared gray man

b.x: This is education. It is not a diagnosis and not a medical order. It does not replace a hands-on course or the ambulance. In Brazil: 192 medical, 193 fire, 190 police. If the scene is not safe, you do not go in. A dead helper saves no one.
The order, always
01 Look at the scene. Wire, fire, water, traffic, an attack, gas. If that is there, move people back and call. Do not become the second victim.
02 Call emergency early. Say where you are, what you see, how many people, whether they breathe. Do not hang up until they say so.
03 Speak to the person. Touch the shoulder. Ask the name. Someone who answers and breathes has already given you half the picture.
04 Do not give water, food, or someone else’s medicine. Do not film instead of calling. Stay until help takes over.
Stroke
Mouth pulled to one side. An arm that will not rise. Slurred speech, a word that will not come, confusion that arrived in an hour. One of these is enough. A sudden, very strong headache counts too.
01 Write the time it started. The hospital uses that number. Time is brain.
02 Call 192. Do not drive them if speech has already failed or they are vomiting. The wrong road loses the minute.
03 Do not give water, food, or aspirin. Choking in the middle of a stroke kills.
04 If they vomit and still breathe, lay them on the side, mouth down. If awake and not vomiting, head slightly raised.
05 Do not wait for it to pass. Many strokes seem to fade and come back worse.
Heart attack

Tightness in the chest, a weight, a burn that is not from food. It can go to the arm, the jaw, the back, the stomach. Cold sweat, nausea, shortness of breath. In a woman, an older person, or someone with diabetes the pain can be slight: sudden fatigue, vomiting, a sickness that will not settle.
01 Stop. Sit them reclined, knees bent if that is easier. Loosen collar and belt. Do not lay them flat if the breath gets worse that way.
02 Call 192. Do not drive in the middle of strong pain. The wheel is not an ambulance.
03 Do not give someone else’s medicine. Aspirin only if emergency tells you, and the person is awake, not allergic, and able to swallow.
04 If they stop answering and are not breathing, start compressions in the center of the chest. A heart attack becomes a cardiac arrest without warning.
Not breathing
They do not answer. The chest does not rise. A snore or a rare gasp is not breathing. Gray skin or blue lips.
01 Shout for help and call 192. Alone with an adult, call first and come back. With a child, do one minute of compressions and call, if the phone is not in your hand.

02 A hard surface. Center of the chest, between the nipples. Adult: two hands, about five to six centimeters, one hundred to one hundred and twenty a minute. The song does not matter. The rhythm does.
03 Child: one hand, less deep. Baby: two fingers in the center of the chest, about four centimeters. Do not press the belly.
04 If you took a course and remember breaths, thirty compressions and two breaths. If you do not remember, hands only. Hands that stop kill more than an imperfect breath.
05 Switch with another person every two minutes if someone is there. Stop only when help takes over, the person truly breathes, or you cannot go on.
Choking
Hands at the throat. Cannot speak. Cannot cough. No air. A strong cough is still protection: do not interrupt it.
01 Ask: are you choking? If they nod and cannot cough, act.

02 Adult: lean them forward. Five blows with the heel of the hand between the shoulder blades. Then five thrusts inward and upward, above the navel. Repeat. Late pregnancy or a very large person: thrust the center of the chest, not the belly.
03 Baby: face down on your forearm, head lower. Five blows on the back. Turn. Five thrusts with two fingers in the center of the chest. Do not shake. Do not sweep a finger blindly in the mouth.
04 If they faint, lay them down and start compressions. Call 192. The object can come out with the chest thrusts.
Fainting
They fell, pale, sweaty, came back or did not. It can be heat, an empty stomach, a fright. It can also be the heart, bleeding inside, or a stroke.
01 Lay them down. If there was no fall from height and no blow to the head, raise the legs. Loosen clothes. Air.
02 Do not throw water on the face. Do not give alcohol, smelling salts, or anything in the mouth until they speak clearly.
03 If they return within a minute, sit them up slowly. Ask about chest pain, breath, pregnancy, diabetes.
04 Call 192 if they do not return soon, if they are older, pregnant, a child, if the head was hit, if there was a seizure, chest pain, or they fainted without warning during effort.
Seizure
Body rigid, shaking, a lost stare, they may bite the tongue and pass urine. It is not possession and it is not a show.
01 Move furniture away. Protect the head with clothing. Do not hold the body down. Do not open the mouth. Do not put in a hand, a spoon, or cloth.
02 Count the time. Most pass in one or two minutes.
03 When it stops, if they breathe, lay them on the side. Stay. They wake confused. Speak low. Do not offer water yet.
04 Call 192 if it is the first, if it passes five minutes, if another follows, if they do not wake, if they are pregnant, injured, or in water.
Bleeding
Blood that will not stop, that soaks the clothes, that jets with the pulse. That outranks a bone and a scream.
01 Direct pressure with a clean cloth, your hand on top. Do not keep lifting it to look. If it soaks through, put another cloth on the first.
02 Lay them down. If the wound is on an arm or a leg and no broken bone is obvious, raise the limb while you press.
03 An object stuck in: do not pull it out. Press at the sides and steady the object with cloth. Pulling it can open what was still holding.
04 A tourniquet is not the first move. Only when the blood jets and pressure is not holding the life, or emergency tells you. Write the time. Do not loosen it later on your own.
Car crash
A crash, a motorcycle, someone hit. The person screaming is not the most serious. The one who goes quiet, who does not answer, is.
01 Your life first. Do not cross the road in the dark unseen. If you can, signal from far, not on top of the wreck.
02 Call 192 and 193. Say the road, the direction, how many vehicles, whether there is fire or a strong smell of fuel.
03 Do not pull out someone who is breathing if there is no fire, smoke, or another car coming. The neck breaks in the hurry to be a hero.
04 Do not remove a helmet. Open the visor if you need to see the mouth. If there is fire and you must move them, head, neck, and trunk come out together, with more than one person.
05 Switch off the ignition if you can reach it without twisting the injured person. Do not give water. Bleeding, no breath, and whoever does not answer go first.
Taken ill
Dizziness, vomiting, confusion, fever, a pain they cannot explain. It can be pressure, sugar, infection, heat, too much medicine, or the start of a heart attack without the classic pain.
01 Sit or lay them down, as the breath allows. Shade if they are in the sun. Do not let them go to the bathroom alone if they are already unsteady.
02 Ask three things: diabetes, allergy, heart medicine. Look for a bracelet and a medical card if they cannot speak.
03 If they are diabetic, awake, and able to swallow, give sugar: juice, honey, ordinary soda. If they cannot swallow, do not force it. Call 192.
04 Call 192 if the confusion grows, the skin turns gray, the pain is in the chest or the head, the fever comes with a stiff neck, or they stop passing urine and grow very weak.
Burn
Fire, oil, steam, chemical, wire. A blister, white skin, cloth stuck on. A child, and a burn on the face, the hand, the genitals, or a large area, are serious even if the person is talking.
01 Stop the fire. Cool running water for twenty minutes. No ice. No toothpaste, butter, coffee, egg white.
02 Do not burst a blister. Do not pull off stuck cloth. Remove a ring and a watch before swelling, if they come off easily.
03 Chemical: long running water, remove contaminated clothes without spreading them onto the face. Electrical: do not touch. Cut the power. Call 192 and 193.
04 Cover with clean cloth, no ointment. Face, a hoarse airway, a child, and a large area: call 192.
Bone and a fall
A limb at a wrong angle, they cannot bear weight, it swells fast. A fall from standing height in an older person can break the hip without a scene.
01 Do not put the bone back. Do not try to snap it. Splint it as it lies, including the joint above and the joint below, if you can do it without extra pain.
02 A finger or a hand that turns purple, cold, with no pulse: call 192 now. The blood is not arriving.
03 A fall with neck pain or tingling in the legs: do not sit them up. Do not remove a helmet. Wait for help, unless there is fire.
04 An older person on the floor, a leg that looks short or turned out: do not stand them up to see if they can walk. Call 192. The hip is not stubbornness.
Severe allergy
Swelling of the mouth, the tongue, the throat. Wheeze. Hives that rise together with a collapse. It can be food, a medicine, a sting. Minutes count.
01 Call 192. Say allergy and shortness of breath.
02 If they carry their own epinephrine pen and were taught to use it, help the way the device says. Do not invent a dose. Do not use someone else’s pen if you do not know.
03 If they vomit or the tongue swells, do not leave them flat on the back without watching the air. On the side, if needed.
04 Even if they improve after the pen, the hospital is required. The reaction returns.
Drowning
A person who is truly drowning almost does not shout. They stay vertical, mouth at the waterline, an arm that does not wave. A quiet child at the edge too.
01 Do not go in if you do not know how to get someone out of the water. One more hero becomes two bodies. Throw something that floats. Call someone who knows.
02 Out of the water, if they are not breathing, start compressions. Do not lose a minute trying to empty the lung upside down.
03 Vomiting is common. Turn them on the side, clear what comes out without a finger sweep, return to the chest if the breath does not come back.
04 Someone who speaks again still goes to the hospital. Water that went in gets worse later.
Too much heat
Confusion in the sun, skin very hot, it may be dry or sweaty. It is not only fatigue. It is an emergency when the person does not make sense.
01 Shade. Lay them down. Remove extra clothes. Water on the skin, a fan, a wet cloth on the neck and the armpits. Call 192.
02 If they are awake and swallowing, water in sips. If they cannot swallow, do not force it.
03 Do not give alcohol. Do not cover them with a blanket. The body needs to lose heat, not keep it.
Snakebite

In Brazil a bite is a hospital, not a backyard recipe. A lancehead hurts and swells. A rattlesnake barely marks and drops the eyelid. A true coral is discreet and takes the breath. A bushmaster, in the North, swells and drops the pressure. You do not need the right name. You need to stop the wrong move and reach the antivenom.

01 Move the person away from the snake. Do not chase it. Do not kill it to carry it. A second bite, on the hand of the one who went to grab it, is common. A photo only from far, if it does not delay leaving. The doctor chooses the antivenom by what the body does, not by the trophy.

02 Write the time. Lay them down. Speak low. Do not let them walk, run, or wave the arm. Movement spreads the venom through the lymph. If there is no car, carry them. The person who was bitten does not walk the trail back on their own feet if there is another way.

03 Wash the spot with soap and water, if you have it, without scrubbing until it bleeds. Remove a ring, a bracelet, a watch, and a tight boot before it swells. Keep the limb still, at the height of the heart. Do not raise it. Do not hang it down.

04 Do not cut. Do not suck. Do not tourniquet. Do not put ice, alcohol, gasoline, kerosene, coffee powder, garlic, dirt, a leaf, or feces. Do not give liquor. Do not give a pain medicine on your own. That delays the antivenom and ruins the arm.

05 Call 192 at once. Do not wait for swelling to see if it was a dry bite. Say the town, the time, and what you see: swelling, bleeding gums, a drooping eyelid, dark urine, shortness of breath. Antivenom exists only in a health service. The corner pharmacy does not sell it.

06 Lanceheads and their kin are the most common. Strong pain, swelling that climbs, a purple patch, a blister, bleeding from the gums or the wound. The danger is blood that will not clot and an arm that tightens inside its own skin.

07 A rattlesnake hurts little at the spot and barely swells. Hours later: a drooping eyelid, double vision, muscle pain, urine the color of coffee. That is an emergency even with a small mark. Do not decide it was nothing because the foot looks fine.

08 A true coral leaves a discreet mark. The venom is of the nerve: slurred speech, saliva, the eyelid, breath that fails. It can take time. Stay with the person. If the chest stops rising, compressions and 192, as in the section for someone who is not breathing.
09 The bushmaster is of the North. Large swelling plus a drop in pressure, vomiting, sweat, diarrhea. Same rule: still, no tourniquet, hospital. It is not an animal to kill in the yard.

10 On the way, if they are awake and not vomiting, they may wet the mouth with water. If the eyelid drops, the speech changes, or they vomit, nothing in the mouth. Lay them on the side if needed. Do not let them sleep with nobody watching the breath.
What this tab refuses
It does not teach surgery, a cut in the throat, or borrowed medicine.
It does not teach removing a helmet, pulling an object from the body, bursting a blister, or sucking venom.
It does not teach filming. The phone is for calling and for the time the stroke started.
It does not replace a course with a manikin and an instructor. Read today. Train with someone who really teaches.
